cards.explanation: The order is to strike the tops of the pillars so the thresholds shake. The Lord says, "Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake. Topple them on the heads of all the people…" (Amos 9:1) I think this is one of those moments where you just hold your breath and keep reading, friends.

The answer is False, and it's a heavy line. The Lord says, "None of those who flee will get away; none of the fugitives will escape." (Amos 9:1) Nobody slips out, not even one. I think that's the whole point of this stretch, friends: there is no running from Him.

The answer is that He will pull them down from there. The Lord says, "…though they climb up to heaven, from there I will pull them down." (Amos 9:2) Down in Sheol, up in heaven, same result. Both directions are covered, friends, and nobody gets a free pass for going the extra mile.

The answer is the serpent. The Lord says, "…there I will command the serpent to bite them." (Amos 9:3) Look where that line lands: "…though they hide from Me at the bottom of the sea…" Even down there, friends, He says they won't be hiding from Him.

The answer is True. The Lord says, "I will fix My eyes upon them for harm and not for good." (Amos 9:4) It's a hard line to read, friends. I think it fits everything before it, because there's no hiding spot left.

The answer is melts. The text says the Lord GOD of Hosts is the One "…who touches the earth and it melts, and all its dwellers mourn…" (Amos 9:5) One touch, and the earth melts. I think that's a good moment, friends, to just sit with how big He is.

The answer is True. The text says, "He summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth." (Amos 9:6) The sea answers when He calls, friends. And then comes the line, "The LORD is His name."

The answer is the Philistines. The LORD says, "Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?" (Amos 9:7) Israel isn't the only people He has brought up from somewhere, friends. I think that's worth sitting with for a minute.

The answer is False, and it's a big turn. The LORD says, "Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob…" (Amos 9:8) The sinful kingdom meets its end, but Jacob's house is not utterly destroyed. I think that "Yet" is where you can finally breathe a little, friends.

The answer is that not one will reach the ground. The LORD says He will shake Israel like grain in a sieve, "but not a pebble will reach the ground." (Amos 9:9) Not one pebble hits the ground, friends. I once lost a whole sprinkle jar down a drain and I'm still not over it.

The answer is those who say disaster will never reach them. The LORD says, "All the sinners among My people will die by the sword—all those who say, ‘Disaster will never draw near or confront us.’…" (Amos 9:10) Those words are the ones He points to, friends. I think it's a good reminder to be careful of saying "it won't happen to me."
